title: Mongolian Beef Stir-Fry
description: Serve this sizzling stir-fry in a cast-iron pan for full restaurant-style drama — the sizzling, spitting finish brings the flavour alive.

ingredients.notes: white and green parts separated, sliced

method.instruction: Combine beef strips with bi-carb soda, 5 g of the cornflour, 15 ml of the light soy sauce, and 15 ml of the Chinese rice wine. Mix well, cover, and set aside for 1 hour to marinate.

Mix the remaining 5 g of cornflour with dark soy sauce and the remaining 5 ml of light soy sauce until smooth, then stir in sambal oelek, oyster sauce, the remaining 15 ml of Chinese rice wine, five spice, and water. Set sauce aside.
Heat vegetable oil and sesame oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Stir-fry onion and the white parts of spring onion for 1 minute. Add garlic and cook for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add marinated beef and stir-fry until no longer red, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and cook until reduced and caramelised, about 3 minutes.
Toss through the green parts of spring onion until just wilted. Serve immediately — ideally in a hot cast-iron pan for a sizzling effect.

notes.title: Bi-Carb Soda Tenderising
notes.content: The bi-carb soda in the marinade is a classic Chinese restaurant technique that tenderises the beef and gives it that signature silky texture. Do not skip it.

notes.title: Recipe Inspiration
notes.content: This Mongolian Beef Stir-Fry draws inspiration from traditional Chinese banquet cooking methods.
